slots.label: A1: Eccentric-accentuated EZ bar or barbell curl
slots.notes: Curl the weight out in front of you. Use a slow 3 second lowering phase

slots.label: A2: Rope overhead triceps extension
slots.notes: Do both arms at once

slots.label: B1: Concentration curl
slots.notes: Keep your forearm as loose as possible, focus on contracting your biceps

slots.label: Pin squat
slots.notes: Set the pins to just above parallel

slots.label: A1: Sissy squat
slots.notes: Or leg press with low foot placement. Let your knees travel forward.

slots.label: Hip abduction
slots.notes: Machine, band, or weighted, 1 second isometric hold at the top of each rep

slots.label: Barbell bench press (RPE 9.5 AMRAP)
slots.notes: Do as many reps as possible to an RPE 9-9.5. Don't actually fail. Use a spotter

slots.label: Barbell bench press (Back off)
slots.notes: Go lighter

slots.label: Machine shoulder press
slots.notes: Do seated DB arnold press if no machine. Push these just shy of failure

slots.label: Close-grip incline barbell bench press
slots.notes: Just outside shoulder width grip

slots.label: Lateral raise (choice)
slots.notes: Can use cable, dumbbell or bands. Stay in constant tension.

slots.label: Chest-supported row
slots.notes: Can use machine or dumbbells.

slots.label: Single-arm pulldown
slots.notes: Start with your weaker side

slots.label: Helms row
slots.notes: Drive elbows out and back at 45 degree angle

slots.label: Bayesian Curl
slots.notes: Keep your arm behind your body throughout the set

slots.label: Inverse Zottman curl
slots.notes: Hammer curl on concentric, supinated curl (palms up) on the eccentric

slots.label: Leg extension
slots.notes: Dropset. Do 15 reps, drop the weight up to 50%, do another 10 reps.

slots.label: Deficit push-up
slots.notes: 4" deficit. Sink your chest deep. Beat your reps from last week.

slots.label: Multi-height cable crossover
slots.notes: Do one set with low cable position, one set with medium-height cable position, one set at high cable position

slots.label: Weighted eccentric-overload pull-up
slots.notes: Jump up to assist with the positive, then control the negative for 5 seconds.

slots.label: Pendlay row / bent over row
slots.notes: First 5 reps: very strict Pendlay rows. Final 10 reps: "cheat" barbell bent over rows (use controlled momentum and pull to stomach)

slots.label: Pinch grip curl
slots.notes: Pinch the end cap of a dumbbell with your hand open, then curl the weight up

readMe: Beginner 12-Week Strength Program
Four options: 2, 3, 4 or 5 strength days a week. Start with Option B (3 days). Same layout as the RW Fitness program files so the app importer can read it.
How to use
1. Pick one option tab. Each week lists every session in order; do them in order, not tied to weekdays.
2. Yellow cells in the Load (kg) column are for you to fill in. Example: Week 1, Goblet squat, 2 sets x 12 reps at 8 kg, RPE 6 -> type 8.
3. When you hit the top of the rep range on every set for two sessions at or below the target RPE, add the smallest weight step next session.
4. Weeks 8 and 12 are easy weeks (2 sets, RPE 6, same weights).
Assumptions
Session length estimates: sets x (40 sec work + rest) + 30 sec per exercise + 6 min warm-up + 5 min cool-down + 3 min ramp-up. Estimates only.
Weights, reps and RPE targets are my programming defaults for a beginner; nothing here is medical advice. Check with a GP before starting.
RPE: 6 = about 4 reps left, 7 = about 3 left, 8 = about 2 left. Do not train to failure.

readMe: Beginner 12-Week Strength Program
Four options: 2, 3, 4 or 5 strength days a week. Start with Option B (3 days). Same layout as the RW Fitness program files so the app importer can read it.
How to use
1. Pick one option tab. Each week lists every session in order; do them in order, not tied to weekdays.
2. Yellow cells in the Load (kg) column are for you to fill in. Example: Week 1, Goblet squat, 2 sets x 12 reps at 8 kg, RPE 6 -> type 8.
3. When you hit the top of the rep range on every set for two sessions at or below the target RPE, add the smallest weight step next session.
4. Weeks 8 and 12 are easy weeks (2 sets, RPE 6, same weights).
Assumptions
Session length estimates: sets x (40 sec work + rest) + 30 sec per exercise + 6 min warm-up + 5 min cool-down + 3 min ramp-up. Estimates only.
Weights, reps and RPE targets are my programming defaults for a beginner; nothing here is medical advice. Check with a GP before starting.
RPE: 6 = about 4 reps left, 7 = about 3 left, 8 = about 2 left. Do not train to failure.

readMe: Beginner 12-Week Strength Program
Four options: 2, 3, 4 or 5 strength days a week. Start with Option B (3 days). Same layout as the RW Fitness program files so the app importer can read it.
How to use
1. Pick one option tab. Each week lists every session in order; do them in order, not tied to weekdays.
2. Yellow cells in the Load (kg) column are for you to fill in. Example: Week 1, Goblet squat, 2 sets x 12 reps at 8 kg, RPE 6 -> type 8.
3. When you hit the top of the rep range on every set for two sessions at or below the target RPE, add the smallest weight step next session.
4. Weeks 8 and 12 are easy weeks (2 sets, RPE 6, same weights).
Assumptions
Session length estimates: sets x (40 sec work + rest) + 30 sec per exercise + 6 min warm-up + 5 min cool-down + 3 min ramp-up. Estimates only.
Weights, reps and RPE targets are my programming defaults for a beginner; nothing here is medical advice. Check with a GP before starting.
RPE: 6 = about 4 reps left, 7 = about 3 left, 8 = about 2 left. Do not train to failure.

readMe: Beginner 12-Week Strength Program
Four options: 2, 3, 4 or 5 strength days a week. Start with Option B (3 days). Same layout as the RW Fitness program files so the app importer can read it.
How to use
1. Pick one option tab. Each week lists every session in order; do them in order, not tied to weekdays.
2. Yellow cells in the Load (kg) column are for you to fill in. Example: Week 1, Goblet squat, 2 sets x 12 reps at 8 kg, RPE 6 -> type 8.
3. When you hit the top of the rep range on every set for two sessions at or below the target RPE, add the smallest weight step next session.
4. Weeks 8 and 12 are easy weeks (2 sets, RPE 6, same weights).
Assumptions
Session length estimates: sets x (40 sec work + rest) + 30 sec per exercise + 6 min warm-up + 5 min cool-down + 3 min ramp-up. Estimates only.
Weights, reps and RPE targets are my programming defaults for a beginner; nothing here is medical advice. Check with a GP before starting.
RPE: 6 = about 4 reps left, 7 = about 3 left, 8 = about 2 left. Do not train to failure.
